clue.text: Be in among the troops in South Wales

indicators.note: the word be is placed in among the letters of the troops, so this phrase signals one piece going inside another

parts.note: artillery is a body of troops manning big guns
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go and live among the soldiers stationed in South Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in among' puts BE inside ARTILLERY. The definition is a place description: the answer is a former mining town in Blaenau Gwent, South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The town lies in the valleys of South Wales, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Note if the parson be about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word be goes round the clergyman's title

parts.note: taken as written
Rev, short for Reverend, is a parson's title

explanation.surface: A remark about whether the parson might be nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts REV inside BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a musical note lasting two semibreves, now rarely used.

clue.text: Coming to a similar conclusion, we hear

definitions.text: Coming to a similar conclusion, we hear

parts.words: Coming to a similar conclusion, we hear
parts.note: words whose endings sound alike to the ear finish in the same way; 'conclusion' means the end of a word, not an agreed opinion

explanation.surface: Two people independently reach the same verdict, or so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming to a similar conclusion' looks like agreement in argument; it means two words ending with the same sound, which is why 'we hear' is there.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse lines that chime share the same final sound, the defining trait of rhyme.

clue.text: Demon wind damage

parts.note: an imp is a small demon
air is moving wind, a breeze

explanation.surface: A demonic wind causes destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or harm it, a synonym of the verb damage.

clue.text: Extended break for a fielder

parts.note: long means extended in length
a stop is a break or pause

explanation.surface: A long holiday taken by a cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the long stop fields directly behind the wicketkeeper, near the boundary, to stop byes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielding position, and the player standing in it, deep behind the wicketkeeper.

clue.text: Again put in order reformed earl taking gin cocktail

indicators.note: reformed means made again in a new shape, so the letters of earl are rearranged
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed

explanation.surface: A nobleman who has mended his ways nonetheless takes a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' makes REAL from EARL and 'cocktail' makes IGN from GIN; 'taking' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to bring things back into a straight line or proper arrangement once more.

clue.text: Press clamours for a fast game

parts.note: to squash is to press flat
rackets are noisy din, clamours

explanation.surface: Journalists make a noise about a quick sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the news media; it is the verb meaning squeeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Squash rackets is the full name of the quick indoor sport played with rackets against walls.

clue.text: Teenager is upset by dressmakers

parts.note: a Mod was a stylish 1960s British teenager on a scooter
taken as written
read as 'set up': in a down clue the word set going up gives its letters bottom to top

explanation.surface: A teenage girl is annoyed by the people making her clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is split as 'set up': in a down entry SET read upwards gives TES. MODS were a 1960s British youth cult.
explanation.definitionFit: A modiste is a fashionable milliner or dressmaker, from the French word.

clue.text: After all is not out of the running

definitions.meaning: still present, still taking part when the race ends

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually, and also describes a contender still there when a race closes.

clue.text: Raising it introduces an element of doubt

definitions.text: Raising it introduces an element of doubt

parts.words: Raising it introduces an element of doubt
parts.note: 'raising' means putting forward a question in a meeting, not lifting something up, and doing so casts doubt on a matter

explanation.surface: Lifting something up brings in uncertainty.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a question about something is to express doubt about it.

clue.text: They are worn endlessly by an absurd old man in pantomime

definitions.text: an absurd old man in pantomime

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the garment word is dropped

parts.note: pantaloons are trousers that are worn

explanation.surface: Baggy trousers are worn by the foolish old character in a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final S. Pantaloon is the foolish old man of the commedia dell'arte and of British Christmas pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantaloon is the stock figure of a foolish elderly man in harlequinade and pantomime.

clue.text: As if tripe could be prepared for starters

indicators.note: preparing food changes it, so the letters are rearranged into a new dish

explanation.surface: Tripe might be cooked up as hors d'oeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be prepared' rearranges AS IF TRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aperitifs are drinks taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite, a beginning to dinner.

clue.text: As a fool I do it badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of these words are put wrongly, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Someone admits they perform clumsily, like a clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges I DO IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton or clown is a stupid person, a synonym of the noun fool.

clue.text: Respect silver found in the home

indicators.note: found in means placed within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as the word home
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Silverware discovered at home earns admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts AG inside HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is public honour or reverence shown to someone.

clue.text: Exclusive control is the name of the game

definitions.meaning: sole command of a market or supply

explanation.definitionFit: The word means sole command of a commodity, and is also a well-known property-trading board game.

clue.text: First-rate spinner not by the church

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
taken as written

explanation.surface: An excellent spin bowler is positioned away from the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch means of the highest quality, excellent.

clue.text: Pine for many with severe mental suffering

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, taken as many
anguish is severe mental pain

explanation.surface: Someone yearns for many things while in deep distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' as L (Roman fifty) is a crossword convention; 'for' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to waste away or long for something, as to pine does.

clue.text: Strange girl in the new lab.

indicators.note: in places the girl's name within the other letters
new signals the letters of lab are remade in a fresh order

parts.note: Norma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An odd young woman is working in the newly built laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes ABL from LAB, and 'in' puts NORMA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means departing from what is usual, odd.

clue.text: Follow one's tracks back on the rickety terrace

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone retraces their steps along a decrepit row of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rickety' rearranges TERRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrace is to go back over the same route again.

clue.text: Main part on condition that it is central France

parts.note: the mass is the main body or bulk of something
if means on condition that

explanation.surface: The bulk of something, provided it lies in the middle of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Massif Central is the upland region of south-central France, so 'it is central France' points to its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact mountain mass, and the Massif Central is France's central upland.

clue.text: Everybody, say, rejecting gold briskly!

parts.note: all means everybody
eg (for example) is signalled by say

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the gold word is turned backwards

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Everyone, for instance, briskly turns down gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns OR into RO. In music the word is a tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is a musical direction meaning quick and lively.

clue.text: Put right in the picture

indicators.note: in places the letter for right within the picture word

parts.note: an inset is a small picture set within a larger one

explanation.surface: Someone is brought up to date, told everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put right in the picture' reads as an idiom for informing someone; 'in' puts R inside INSET.
explanation.definitionFit: To insert is to put something into a place.

clue.text: King with a set not working

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
to set is to put

explanation.surface: A king with his television set that has broken down.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput is slang for broken, finished, out of order.

clue.text: Information let outby one per person, male

parts.note: gen is slang for information

indicators.note: printed run together for 'out by'; out means unconventional, so the letters of let are rearranged

parts.note: man means a person

explanation.surface: Information released one per person, for men only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' (printed run together with 'by' as 'outby') rearranges LET into TLE; 'one per' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman is a man, a polite term for a male person.

clue.text: Tree, palm moved alongside the point

indicators.note: moved signals the letters of palm shift into another order

parts.note: E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: A palm tree is moved next to a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges PALM into MAPL.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a deciduous tree, source of syrup.

clue.text: Chatty lecture at tea-time perhaps by egghead

parts.note: a talk is a lecture
taken as written
four o'clock, IV in Roman numerals, is a traditional time for afternoon tea
the head, or first letter, of egg

explanation.surface: A lecture given at teatime by an intellectual turns out to be gossipy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual; it gives the first letter of EGG. Four o'clock is British teatime, IV in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Talkative means fond of conversation, inclined to chat a lot.

clue.text: Looks at the pages turned over

indicators.note: turned over here means jumbled about, so the letters of pages are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stares at the pages being turned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' rearranges PAGES; it looks like a reversal, but the word read backwards does not give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stare open-mouthed, so gapes means stares or looks.

clue.text: Plant might be taken out of the fire

definitions.text: Plant might be taken out of the fire

parts.words: Plant might be taken out of the fire
parts.note: a garden flower named after a glowing iron rod for stirring coals, as one pulled from the flames would be

explanation.surface: A plant is rescued from a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: The kniphofia, with spikes of red and yellow flowers, is named after a fire iron glowing from the coals.
explanation.definitionFit: The kniphofia is a tall garden plant whose flame-coloured spikes resemble a glowing fire iron.
